title: Götzendämmerung: Kunst und Künstliche Intelligenz

description.main: A German-language volume on the changing relationship between artists and machines, edited by Bernhard J. Dotzler and Berkan Karpat. It documents an exhibition series at the Haus der Kunst Munich and was published by transcript in 2021.
description.extended:
A German-language volume on art and artificial intelligence that asks what remains of the artistic act once attention shifts from artists to the machine process.

The editors observe that the focus has moved from artists to the mechanical process, reducing the artistic act to averaging data structures. The book documents an exhibition series at the House of Art in Munich and looks at how art increasingly meets political and social spaces while new aesthetic dynamics form between people and technology. Contents include a foreword, a 50-page section titled "Life's but a walking shadow," essays on computational creativity, algorithmic emotion and human-machine relations, artist statements and appendices. It runs 154 pages and appeared from transcript Verlag on 15 September 2021, in the series KI-Kritik / AI Critique.

Dotzler teaches at the University of Regensburg and Karpat works at the House of Art Munich.
